correctness.rationale: All projective cubics are exhausted by 29524 scalar-normalized coefficient vectors; exact all-three-chart Groebner unit-ideal tests give 936 smooth blocking equations, one 936-element PGL3(F3) orbit, and six rational points each. For a fixed member F, normalization G(P0)=1 and G_X^3=0 gives a one-to-one listing of all 3^8 pencils through F with no rational base points. Exactly 864 pass basepoint conditions and 312 have the other three members geometrically smooth; independent finite-field and Groebner implementations return identical 312 coefficient lists and (24,132,42,114) counts. At most one blocking member follows from the 13-point partition, the six-point lower bound for smooth blocking cubics, and at least one rational point on any smooth plane cubic. Hence each global pencil counted once, giving 936*312=292032. All finite loops and geometric claims are encoded in package source files; no sampling is used.

originality.rationale: Published work separates the existence of all-smooth pencils, exceptional small-field smooth blocking cubics, and general nonblocking lower bounds. It does not yield the exact number 292032 of basepoint-free all-smooth cubic pencils with a blocking member or the four partition profiles. Same-paper open-access comparison and actual mathematical-record searches revealed no dominating theorem or exact table. An unindexed computational catalogue remains a stated publication-priority risk; absence from search alone is not the reason for PASS.
residual_risks: Unindexed or older small-field pencil catalogues could have recorded an equivalent exact incidence distribution.
The complete body of every potentially related older textbook/table was not available; priority is not externally certified.

value.rationale: This finite classification resolves a natural first odd-field intersection of all-rational-member smoothness, rational-basepoint-free pencil structure, and exceptional blocking. It sharpens the general pencil guarantee from two to three nonblocking members under a genuine geometric hypothesis, proves attainability and counts every equality pencil together with four distinct fiber point-count spectra. The exact mass/profile is not merely a change of notation or an arbitrary coefficient slice, and requires a complete global-to-local incidence analysis.
